description.narrative: There has been an outbreak of Mpox, also known Monkeypox, in Uganda. As of 19 August, the Ministry of Health (MoH) of Uganda had confirmed 3 cases, two of them from Kasese district out of 39 suspected cases and one in Kampala. Additionally, in West Nile a total of 10 suspected cases (Arua – 2, Madi Okollo – 1, Terego - 5 and Yumbe – 2) and in Kyegegwa a total of 14 alert were received, out ofwhich 10 samples tested 8 negative and the 2 are pending results. As a result, the MoH activated the national task force team and is implementing the Uganda National Mpox Preparedness and Response Plan alongside its partners. Inter-agency health and other partners are working in line with the national response, as well as monitoring for any potential negative messaging about refugees considering the linkages to cross-border transmission from DRC with limited resources. The ministry of health has appealed to partners to extend in risk communication and community engagement, infection prevention and control – WaSH among others. Uganda receives businesspeople and truck drivers from DRC to Kampala for trade, sizable number of pupils attending schools. Uganda receives and hosts over 1.59 million refugees and 46,104 asylum seekers in the 13 settlements in the districts of Koboko, Yumbe, Obongi, Adjumani, Lamwo, Terego, Madi-okollo, Kiryandongo, Kikuube, Kamwenge, Kyegegwa, Isingiro and the urban settlement in Kampala. Other activity refugee receiving districts are Kisoro, Kanungu, Kasese, Bundibugyo, Ntoroko, Kikuube. Since start of the year 2024, Uganda has received close to 66,193 refugees of which 20% (13,310/66,193) are from the DRC. This greatly increases the risk of transmission of Mpox to Uganda exacerbated by the continuous influx of refugees from the North and South Kivu war affected regions. The recent evidence of sexual transmission from the predominately male to female has increased the risk of Mpox transmission. This increases the risk of importationand transmission through sexual networks mainly among refugees and minority communities residing more in preurban and urban centers. This also increases the risk of cross boarder transmission through designated and undesignated boarder points. this therefore increases the risk of importation and transmission ofthe disease majorly through fluid and body contacts through sexual networks mainly among the minority communities residing more in preurban and urban centers in the refugee hosting and receiving districts. In Ugandacategorized risky districts as follows: category I districts as border districts that receive a high number of cross-border populations seeking services in Uganda. They host many patients seeking healthcare and children under 15 attending school in Uganda. They include Kisoro, Kanungu, Ntoroko, Bundibugyo, Kikuube, Hoima, Buliisa, Rukungiri, Kasese, Rubirizi and Kampala Metropolitan Area. Category II districts as those with direct links with the affected health zone of North Kivu province and refugee hosting close to the affected area which include Isingiro, Kamwenge, Kyegegwa, Kyenjojo, Kagadi, Pakwach, Kabale, Mbarara, Masaka and Category III districts as those with direct links with DRC but not with North Kivu provinces, and other refugee hosting districts; Nebbi, Zombo, Yumbe,Moyo, Adjumani, Koboko, Arua, Obongi, Lamwo, Madi-Okollo, Terego. Additionally, cities with high connectivity with the affected areas in DRC. Therefore, there is a need for heighted preparedness and response readiness to a potential Mpox outbreak in Uganda.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
